B. Farmers who once sold only at local markets can now ship fruit and tea directly to buyers in coastal cities.
C. Live-streaming sessions hosted by local officials have helped promote regional specialties.
D. Yet poor cold-chain logistics still cause substantial losses of perishable produce.◆Growers can now reach distant urban customers without relying on nearby markets.
B 段说农民过去只在本地集市卖货，如今可直接把水果和茶叶发给沿海城市的买家。

A. Loneliness is increasingly recognized as a public health issue rather than a private misfortune.
B. Research links chronic isolation to higher risks of heart disease and cognitive decline.
C. In 2018 the UK appointed a minister specifically responsible for tackling loneliness.
D. Community programs pairing students with elderly residents have shown promising results.◆One government created a dedicated official post to address the problem.
C 段提到英国任命了专门负责应对孤独问题的大臣，即设立专门官职。

A. Microplastics have been detected in Arctic snow, deep-sea sediments and even human blood.
B. Their health effects on humans remain uncertain because long-term studies are lacking.
C. Some researchers are developing enzymes that can break down common plastics within days.
D. Environmental groups argue that reducing plastic production matters more than cleanup technology.◆Certain campaigners believe cutting output is more important than technical solutions.
D 段说环保团体认为减少塑料生产比清理技术更重要，与陈述一致。

A. Electric vehicles accounted for nearly a third of new car sales in some markets last year.
B. The expansion of charging stations, however, has lagged behind in rural areas.
C. Battery prices have fallen sharply, making electric cars more affordable to middle-income families.
D. Recycling used batteries is emerging as a new industry with significant commercial potential.◆In certain markets, close to one in three newly purchased cars is electric.
A 段说某些市场电动车占新车销量近三分之一，与“近三分之一新车是电动车”一致。

A. Bilingual children often perform better on tasks requiring them to switch attention between rules.
B. Some studies, however, have failed to replicate this so-called bilingual advantage.
C. Researchers suggest the inconsistency may stem from differences in how bilingualism is defined.
D. Regardless of cognitive effects, speaking two languages clearly offers cultural and economic benefits.◆Contradictory findings may result from varying definitions used by researchers.
C 段说结果不一致可能源于对“双语”定义的差异，与陈述对应；B 段只说未能复现。

A. The Grand Canal, stretching nearly 1,800 kilometers, once carried grain from southern China to the capital.
B. Its construction spanned many centuries and involved millions of laborers.
C. Since being listed as a World Heritage Site in 2014, sections of it have been restored for tourism.
D. Scholars note that the canal also encouraged cultural exchange between the north and the south.◆The waterway was once used to transport food supplies to the seat of government.
A 段说大运河曾把南方粮食运往都城，seat of government 即都城。

A. Smart home devices promise convenience by learning residents' daily routines.
B. Privacy advocates warn that such devices collect vast amounts of personal data.
C. Manufacturers say data are encrypted and used only to improve services.
D. A recent survey found that most users never read the privacy terms before installation.◆Critics are concerned about the sheer volume of personal information household gadgets gather.
B 段说隐私倡导者警告此类设备收集大量个人数据，与陈述一致；C 段是厂商的辩护。

A. Coral reefs cover less than one percent of the ocean floor but support about a quarter of marine species.
B. Rising water temperatures cause corals to expel the algae that give them color, a process known as bleaching.
C. Scientists are breeding heat-resistant corals in laboratories to replant damaged reefs.
D. Local fishing communities often depend on healthy reefs for both food and income.◆Warmer seas can cause corals to lose their color.
B 段解释水温升高导致珊瑚排出赋予其颜色的藻类，即白化现象。

A. Gap years, common in Britain, are becoming more popular among Chinese high school graduates.
B. Advocates say time off helps students clarify their interests before choosing a major.
C. Parents often worry that a break will cause their children to fall behind peers.
D. Universities increasingly allow admitted students to defer enrollment for one year.◆Supporters believe a break helps students work out what they want to study.
B 段说支持者认为休整有助于学生在选专业前明确兴趣，与陈述对应。

A. Citizen science projects invite ordinary people to collect data on birds, weather and air quality.
B. Such projects have produced datasets far larger than professional teams could gather alone.
C. Critics question the reliability of data recorded by untrained volunteers.
D. Organizers address this by providing online training and cross-checking submissions.◆Measures have been taken to improve the accuracy of amateur contributions.
D 段说组织者通过在线培训和交叉核对提升数据可靠性，即采取措施提高业余数据的准确性。

For decades, economists assumed that people make financial decisions rationally, weighing costs and benefits. Behavioral economics has challenged this view by showing that choices are heavily shaped by how options are framed. For instance, employees are far more likely to save for retirement when enrollment in a pension plan is automatic rather than optional. Such 'nudges' cost governments little, yet critics worry they may manipulate citizens without their knowledge. Proponents counter that every choice is framed in some way, so the real question is whether the framing serves people's interests.◆What is the main finding of behavioral economics mentioned in the passage?
The way choices are presented strongly influences decisions.
People always weigh costs and benefits carefully.
Governments should make pension plans compulsory.
Financial decisions are mainly driven by income levels.
第二句指出选择在很大程度上受呈现方式（framing）影响；B 是被挑战的传统观点，C、D 文中未提及。

Sleep scientists have long known that teenagers' biological clocks shift later during puberty. Yet most secondary schools still begin classes before 8 a.m., forcing students to wake when their bodies are primed for sleep. When several districts in the United States delayed start times by about an hour, attendance improved and car accidents involving teenage drivers declined. Opponents cite the cost of rearranging bus schedules and after-school activities. Still, many researchers argue that the benefits to health and learning far outweigh such logistical inconveniences.◆What happened after some school districts delayed their start times?
第三句说推迟上学时间后出勤率提高、交通事故减少；B 与反对者所说的成本相反，C、D 无依据。

The rise of remote work has prompted a quiet exodus from expensive city centers. Freed from daily commutes, many professionals have relocated to smaller towns where housing is cheaper and green space more abundant. Local businesses in these towns have enjoyed a boost, but long-term residents sometimes complain that newcomers drive up property prices. Urban economists caution that if the trend persists, city centers could face falling tax revenues just as they need to invest in public transport.◆Why might city centers face difficulties if the trend continues?
They may lose tax income while needing to fund public transport.
They may become too crowded with returning commuters.
Their property prices may rise sharply.
Their local businesses may grow too quickly.
末句指出城市中心可能在需要投资公共交通时面临税收下降；B、C、D 与文意相反或张冠李戴。

Glaciers in the Himalayas supply water to nearly two billion people downstream. As temperatures rise, these glaciers are shrinking faster than at any time in recorded history. In the short term, increased meltwater may actually swell rivers and cause floods. Over the coming decades, however, reduced glacier mass is likely to leave rivers lower during dry seasons, threatening agriculture and hydropower. Scientists stress that regional cooperation in water management is essential, since rivers cross national borders.◆According to the passage, what is the long-term effect of shrinking Himalayan glaciers?
Rivers may carry less water during dry seasons.
Rivers will flood more frequently every year.
第四句说长期来看冰川减少会使旱季河流水位降低；B 是短期影响，C 与原文相反，D 未提及。

Many people believe that multitasking makes them more productive. Cognitive research suggests otherwise: the brain does not truly perform two demanding tasks at once but switches rapidly between them, losing time and accuracy with each switch. Heavy multitaskers, ironically, tend to perform worse on tests of attention than those who focus on one task at a time. The illusion of efficiency persists partly because switching feels stimulating, rewarding us with a sense of busyness.◆What does cognitive research reveal about multitasking?
The brain switches between tasks, losing efficiency each time.
The brain can handle two demanding tasks simultaneously.
Switching tasks takes no measurable time.
第二句说大脑并非同时处理两项任务，而是快速切换并损失时间和准确性；B、C、D 均与原文相反。

Museums around the world are facing growing pressure to return artifacts taken during the colonial era. Some institutions argue that their collections allow millions of visitors to appreciate world cultures in one place. Critics reply that this argument conveniently ignores how the objects were acquired. In recent years, several European museums have returned bronzes and sculptures to their countries of origin, a shift that would have been unthinkable a generation ago. The debate is ultimately about who has the right to tell a culture's story.◆What argument do some museums make for keeping their collections?
Collections let large audiences appreciate diverse cultures in one place.
The objects were all acquired legally.
Countries of origin cannot preserve the artifacts.
Visitors prefer to see original objects abroad.
第二句说这些藏品能让数百万观众在一个地方欣赏世界文化；其他选项是常见论点但文中未提。

Lab-grown meat, produced by cultivating animal cells in bioreactors, has been hailed as a solution to the environmental costs of livestock farming. Early studies suggest it could greatly reduce land use and water consumption. However, the energy required to maintain sterile production conditions is considerable, and if that energy comes from fossil fuels, the climate benefits may shrink. Moreover, consumer acceptance remains uncertain; surveys show many people are uneasy about eating meat that has never been part of an animal.◆What could reduce the climate benefits of lab-grown meat?
Relying on fossil fuels to power production.
Using too much land for bioreactors.
第三句指出维持无菌条件需要大量能源，若来自化石燃料，气候效益会缩小；B、C 与原文相反。

Language extinction is accelerating: linguists estimate that one language disappears roughly every few weeks. When a language dies, it takes with it unique knowledge about local plants, medicine and history. Revitalization efforts, such as immersion schools for children, have succeeded in some communities, notably among the Maori of New Zealand. Such success depends less on funding than on whether younger generations see the language as relevant to their lives.◆What is lost when a language disappears, according to the passage?
Unique knowledge about local nature, healing and the past.
The ability of children to attend school.
第二句说语言消亡会带走关于当地植物、医药和历史的独特知识；其他选项无依据。

Such success depends less on funding than on whether younger generations see the language as relevant to their lives.◆What is the key to successful language revitalization?

Making the language compulsory for adults.

Social media platforms rely on algorithms that prioritize content likely to keep users engaged. Because emotionally charged posts attract more clicks, these systems may inadvertently amplify outrage and misinformation. Some governments have proposed requiring companies to disclose how their algorithms rank content. Tech firms object that such disclosure would expose trade secrets and allow bad actors to game the system. A middle path, some scholars suggest, is to grant vetted independent researchers access to platform data.◆Why might social media algorithms spread misinformation?
They favor emotionally provocative content that attracts clicks.
They are designed to promote false information deliberately.
Governments require them to rank posts by popularity.
Users prefer reading neutral news reports.
第二句说情绪化内容点击多，算法可能无意中放大愤怒与错误信息；B 中 deliberately 与 inadvertently 矛盾。

Volunteering is usually framed as an act of generosity toward others. Yet a growing body of research indicates that volunteers themselves reap substantial benefits. Older adults who volunteer regularly report lower rates of depression and, in some studies, live longer than their peers. Researchers believe the effect arises from a sense of purpose and expanded social networks. Notably, the benefits appear only when volunteering is motivated by concern for others rather than by self-interest.◆What explains the benefits volunteers receive, according to researchers?
A sense of purpose and wider social connections.
第四句说效果源于目标感和扩大的社交网络；其他选项文中未提及。

The traditional view of creativity holds that original ideas strike suddenly, in a flash of inspiration. Historians of science paint a different picture. Most breakthroughs, they argue, emerge from long periods of incremental work, conversation and failed attempts. Even famous 'eureka' moments often turn out, on closer inspection, to have been preceded by years of preparation. Recognizing this, some companies now encourage employees to share half-formed ideas rather than wait for a perfect insight.◆What do historians of science believe about breakthroughs?
They usually result from long periods of gradual work.
They arise suddenly from flashes of inspiration.
They are mostly achieved by individuals working alone.
第三句说大多数突破来自长期渐进的工作、交流和失败尝试；B 是被质疑的传统看法。

In many Chinese cities, community canteens for the elderly have opened in recent years, offering affordable, nutritious meals. They help reduce loneliness among older people.
They train elderly people to cook.
第四句说食堂成了聊天交友的场所，缓解了老年孤独感；其他选项未提及。

Antibiotic resistance occurs when bacteria evolve to survive the drugs designed to kill them. The overuse of antibiotics in both medicine and agriculture has accelerated this process. Without new drugs, routine surgeries and minor infections could once again become life-threatening. Yet pharmaceutical companies have little incentive to develop new antibiotics, because such drugs are used sparingly to prevent resistance and thus generate modest profits. Some experts propose that governments offer financial rewards for successful new antibiotics regardless of sales volume.◆Why are drug companies reluctant to develop new antibiotics?
New antibiotics are used sparingly and earn limited profits.
Bacteria no longer respond to any medicine.
Such drugs are too dangerous to test.
第四句说新抗生素为防止耐药被谨慎使用，利润有限；其他选项无依据。

Handwriting is rapidly giving way to typing in classrooms. Some educators see no cause for concern, arguing that keyboard skills are more useful in the modern workplace. Neuroscientists, however, have found that writing by hand activates brain regions associated with memory more strongly than typing does. Students who take notes by hand tend to summarize ideas in their own words, whereas typists are more inclined to transcribe lectures verbatim. The difference may explain why handwritten notes often lead to better conceptual understanding.◆How do students who take notes by hand differ from those who type?
They tend to rephrase ideas in their own words.
They write down lectures word for word.
They rely more on keyboard shortcuts.
第四句说手写者倾向用自己的话概括，打字者更倾向逐字记录；B 描述的是打字者。

To stimulate domestic consumption and employment.
To reduce noise in residential areas.
第三句说政策旨在促进国内消费并为小商贩创造就业。

Space agencies and private companies are racing to return humans to the Moon, this time with plans for a permanent presence. Water ice discovered at the lunar poles could be converted into drinking water, oxygen and even rocket fuel. Advocates argue that a lunar base would serve as a stepping stone to Mars. Skeptics question whether the enormous costs are justified when pressing problems on Earth remain unsolved. It could be turned into essential resources such as oxygen and fuel.
It proves that life once existed on the Moon.
It makes the Moon easier to see from Earth.
It can be sold to countries on Earth.
第二句说月球冰可转化为饮用水、氧气甚至火箭燃料。

Many people assume that a larger number of choices leads to greater satisfaction. Later studies show the effect is not universal, being strongest when options are hard to compare.◆What did the jam experiment show?
Fewer options led to more purchases.
第二句说提供 6 种果酱时购买率远高于 24 种；B 与结果相反。

Rewilding, the practice of restoring ecosystems by reintroducing species and letting nature take its course, is gaining support across Europe. 第三句说农民报告羊群损失并要求赔偿；B 文中说的是鹿破坏森林。

Digital currencies issued by central banks are being tested in several countries, including China. Unlike cryptocurrencies such as Bitcoin, these currencies are backed by the state and maintain a stable value. Supporters say they can lower transaction costs and bring banking services to people without bank accounts.
